## 3. The substantive content: a change to two reportable segments

From FY2027 Microsoft will report **two** reportable segments, replacing the **three** legacy
segments used throughout the FY2026 10-K and the Q3 FY2026 10-Q:

| Legacy segment (through FY2026) | New FY2027 segment |
|---|---|
| — | **1. Agents and Infra** |
| — | **2. Devices and Consumer** |

The three legacy segments — Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More
Personal Computing — **do not map one-for-one** onto the two new ones. PBP and Intelligent Cloud
substantially consolidate into Agents and Infra, while device and consumer elements move to
Devices and Consumer. **The 8-K does not provide a recast historical bridge**, so FY2027
segment reporting will not be comparable to the FY2026 and prior presentation without one.

**Diligence read:** this materially reduces comparability of Microsoft's historical segment
disclosure. A buyer underwriting segment-level growth must rebuild the series on the new basis
before drawing any trend conclusion. Azure, M365, LinkedIn, GitHub and Dynamics all land in
Agents and Infra, which will become the dominant segment and will inherit the AI infrastructure
cost base.
## 4. Exhibit 99.1 — FURNISHED, NOT FILED (critical)

The 8-K body states that Exhibit 99.1 is being **furnished** to the SEC, and that the
information **shall not be deemed to be "filed"** for the purposes of **Section 18 of the
Securities Exchange Act of 1934** (as amended), and **shall not be incorporated by reference**
into any registration statement or other filing, in each case unless expressly stated.

This follows **General Instruction B.2 to Form 8-K** — the safe harbour for voluntary
disclosure. Concretely, and this is the trap to avoid:

- The recast two-segment financials and the "Investor Metrics" contained in Exhibit 99.1 are
**not part of the audited reporting record**.
- They are **not** subject to Section 18 liability and carry a **lower** standard of assurance
than filed information.
- They are **furnished on a voluntary basis** and Microsoft may change or withdraw them.
- **Any memo statement treating the recast segment data as audited, as "filed", or as
incorporated into the 10-K/10-Q record is an audit finding.** The recast figures belong in a
clearly labelled *management discussion / forward-looking* section, sourced to the 8-K
Item 7.01 and to Exhibit 99.1 as furnished, and never to the audited financial statements.

The same caution applies to any forward-looking content in the investor materials: it is
provided under the SEC's safe harbour and is subject to the risk factors in the 10-K.

- **No recast historical segment financials** bridging the three legacy segments to the two new
ones. NOT DISCLOSED in the 8-K.
- **No restatement** of prior periods is proposed or made. The FY2026 10-K and Q3 FY2026 10-Q
stand on the three-segment basis. NOT DISCLOSED.
- **No effective transition date within FY2027**, no quarterly phasing of the change, and no
restatement policy for segment allocations. NOT DISCLOSED in the 8-K.
- **No change to the CODM measure or to how segment operating income will be allocated.**
NOT DISCLOSED. This matters: the reported segments had different economic profiles

(PBP at a 59.9% operating margin in FY2026 versus MPC at 26.6%), and the basis of
allocation between the two new segments determines how profit will be reported.
- **No quantified revenue or operating income for either new segment.** NOT DISCLOSED.
- **No incremental segment-level disclosure commitments.** NOT DISCLOSED.
- The financial statements themselves are **not** part of an 8-K. NOT APPLICABLE.

**Source:** `filings/current/10-K.txt` (Note 14 — Contingencies, line 7589; Item 3 Legal

## 1. THE HEADLINE ITEM: $28.9 billion IRS transfer pricing assessment

This is, on the disclosed figures, **the single largest quantified contingent liability in
Microsoft's filings** — larger than the entire annual dividend, larger than two years of the
entire buyback programme, and roughly 21% of FY2026 net income before penalties and interest.
**Verbatim substance** (10-K, Note 14 — Contingencies, line 7589):

> "We remain under audit by the IRS for tax years 2014 to 2017. With respect to the audit for
> tax years 2004 to 2013, on September 26, 2023, we received Notices of Proposed Adjustment
> ('NOPAs') from the IRS. The primary issues in the NOPAs relate to intercompany
> transfer pricing. In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of
> **$28.9 billion plus penalties and interest**. As of June 30, 2026, we believe our allowances
> for income tax contingencies are adequate. We disagree with the proposed adjustments and will
> vigorously contest the NOPAs through the IRS's administrative appeals office and, if
> necessary, judicial proceedings."

**Replicated in the 10-Q** at three separate places (lines 4753, 7452, 8126), confirming it
remains a live, current disclosure as of the quarter ended March 31, 2026 — not a stale
year-end disclosure.
### The facts that matter for diligence

| Attribute | Detail | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Disputing authority | **Internal Revenue Service (US)** | 10-K Note 14 |
| Periods under audit | **tax years 2014 to 2017** | 10-K Note 14 |
| Periods assessed | **tax years 2004 to 2013** | 10-K Note 14 |
| Date of NOPAs | **September 26, 2023** | 10-K Note 14 |
| Principal issue | **intercompany transfer pricing** | 10-K Note 14 |
| Amount sought | **$28.9 billion plus penalties and interest** | 10-K Note 14 |

| Tax years 2018+ | **not** under NOPA on the matters described | NOT DISCLOSED |
| Consequential damages / other relief sought | **NOT DISCLOSED** | — |
| Total accrued reserve for the NOPA | **NOT DISCLOSED** as a discrete figure | — |
### Scale and materiality (partner arithmetic)

- **$28.9B vs FY2026 net income of $133,749M** = **21.6% of a full year's net income**, before
penalties and interest which are additional and unquantified.
- **$28.9B vs FY2026 total stockholders' equity of $442,387M** = **6.5% of book equity.**
- **$28.9B vs total cash and short-term investments of $78,272M** (3/31/2026) = **36.9%** of the
entire liquid balance.
- **$28.9B vs FY2026 operating cash flow of $182,935M** = **15.8%** of a year's operating cash
generation.
- **$28.9B vs the entire $743,821M contractual obligations total** = 3.9%.

- **$28.9B vs $40.6B remaining buyback authorisation** = **71%** of the remaining programme.
- For scale, the NOPA is **larger than the whole of Microsoft's FY2026 R&D spend** ($35,562M)
by 81%, and larger than FY2026 dividends and buybacks combined ($16.7B buyback plus dividends)
by a wide margin.

**The exposure is therefore best characterised as a balance-sheet and capital-allocation event
rather than an earnings event.** A loss, if it crystallised, would not impair operating
performance but would consume more than two-thirds of the remaining buyback authorisation and
over a third of the liquid position.
## 2. The audit treatment — a Critical Audit Matter

**This is the strongest available corroboration of the severity.** The 10-K discloses that the
independent auditor identified this matter as a **Critical Audit Matter**, which under
PCAOB/AS 6101 requires the auditor to determine it is **critical to the audit** — that is, a
matter of such magnitude that it required a high degree of auditor judgment and created the
most significant risk of material misstatement.

From the 10-K, Critical Audit Matter disclosure (line 9316) and the associated
**long-term income taxes** note:

- The long-term income taxes liability includes uncertain tax positions relating to
**transfer pricing**.
- Microsoft has **settled a portion** of the IRS audits.
- **Resolution of the remaining matters could have a material impact on the financial
statements.**
**Auditor:** **Deloitte & Touche LLP**, Seattle, Washington. **Report dated July 29, 2026.**

**Diligence read:** an auditor designating a matter as a Critical Audit Matter is an explicit
signal of unusually high estimation uncertainty. Combined with management's own statement that
resolution "could have a material impact on the financial statements", this is a
**first-order diligence item**, not a footnote. Any acquisition structure should be tested for
successor liability on these open tax years, and the specific indemnities/escrows should be
sized against a $28.9B headline plus unquantified penalties and interest.
## 3. Management's position and procedural posture

- Management believes its **allowances for income tax contingencies are adequate** as of
June 30, 2026 (10-K) and as of the March 31, 2026 quarter end (10-Q).
- Microsoft **disagrees** with the proposed adjustments.
- Microsoft intends to **vigorously contest** through the **IRS administrative appeals office**
and, if necessary, **judicial proceedings**.
- **The 10-Q states Microsoft does not expect a final resolution within the next 12 months**
and does not anticipate a **significant increase or decrease** in the contingency within
12 months.

**ASSUMPTION (flagged):** the "no significant increase or decrease" statement is a standard
reserved-matter formulation. It should **not** be read as management forecasting a low
probability of an adverse outcome. The correct reading is only that no *change in the
recorded estimate* is expected — it says nothing about whether the recorded estimate is
adequate. The recorded estimate itself is **NOT DISCLOSED** as a discrete number in the
sections reviewed, so no probability-weighted accrual can be independently verified.
## 4. Other tax exposures disclosed

| Item | Detail | Source | Materiality |
|---|---|---|---|
| Non-US income tax | Subject to income tax in many jurisdictions outside the US | 10-K Note 14 | — |
| Local country audits | Some currently under audit by local tax authorities | 10-K Note 14 | Resolution **"not expected to be material"** |
| **Ireland** | Operations remain subject to examination for **tax years 2021 and onward** | 10-K Note 14 | **NOT DISCLOSED** as a separate exposure |
| US statutory vs effective rate | Effective rate materially below the US statutory rate, driven by foreign rate differentials and credits | 10-K Item 7 | Structural |

**Ireland is worth a specific flag.** Microsoft's largest international tax exposure by
jurisdiction is a multi-year examination open from 2021 onward, running concurrently with the
US transfer pricing dispute. The filing states other local audits are not expected to be
material but makes **no separate materiality statement for Ireland**. Recorded as
**NOT DISCLOSED** and raised as a question for the deal team. Ireland also likely interacts
with the transfer pricing allocation given Microsoft's Irish legal-entity structure — a point
the filings do not address.
## 5. Anti-double-counting note — reserved matters

Line 7585 of the 10-K, immediately preceding the NOPA disclosure, shows amounts of **$24,729M**
and **$22,760M**. These sit in the unrecognized tax benefits / contingency roll-forward and
relate to the **same transfer pricing matters**. **The memo must not present the $28.9B NOPA and
these balance-sheet amounts as two separate exposures** — the NOPA is the IRS's *claim*; the
accrued reserve is Microsoft's *recorded position*, and the relationship between them is not
disclosed. **ASSUMPTION-flagged: I have not traced the roll-forward**, and the checker should
confirm the relationship before either figure is characterised.
**10-K Item 3 (Legal Proceedings, line 980) is a pure cross-reference:**

> "Refer to Note 14 – Contingencies of the Notes to Financial Statements (Part II, Item 8 of
> this Form 10-K) for information regarding legal proceedings in which we are involved."

Item 3 therefore discloses **nothing on its own**; all litigation disclosure sits in Note 14,
which (per the sections reviewed) is dominated by the tax controversy. **10-K Item 4 (Mine
Safety Disclosures) is "Not applicable."**

**NOT DISCLOSED:** no quantified accrual for litigation, no named plaintiffs or claims, no
antitrust or regulatory penalty amounts, and no environmental reserve are disclosed in the
sections reviewed. **FLAG FOR CHECKER:** the 10-K risk factors reference regulatory, antitrust
and platform-competition exposure; whether any of it is accrued is not established by the
material reviewed. A substantive Item 3 is unusual for a company of Microsoft's size and profile
and the reliance on Note 14 should be verified as complete rather than assumed.
## 7. What is NOT DISCLOSED — summary for the memo

- The **accrued reserve** against the NOPA, as a discrete figure.
- **Penalties and interest** — unquantified, and additional to the $28.9B.
- Any **consequential damages**, **secondary liability**, or **successor-transferee** exposure.
- Whether the **2018–2026 open years** are at risk on the same transfer pricing theories. The
NOPA covers 2004–2013; the 2014–2017 audit is unresolved and unquantified.
- **Transfer pricing methodology** for the relevant years and the amount of the adjustment
proposed beyond the headline, by jurisdiction.
- The **probability or expected outcome** of the appeal. NOT DISCLOSED. Do not infer one.
- A separate materiality assessment for the **Ireland 2021+** examination.

## 1. Strategic and competitive risks (line 624)

- **Intense competition across all markets**, from diversified global companies with
significant R&D resources to small specialised firms. **Barriers to entry are low in many of
our businesses** and markets evolve rapidly with disruptive technology.
- **Platform-ecosystem competition.** Microsoft competes with firms offering competing
platforms; a vertically-integrated competitor (single firm controlling hardware and software)
has succeeded in PCs, tablets, smartphones, consoles and wearables, and can earn services
revenue through integrated marketplaces. **Microsoft's own expansion of vertically-integrated
capabilities, including proprietary hardware, infrastructure and AI models, could increase its

cost structure, reduce margins, and expose it to operational risks.** This is a
self-acknowledged strategic tension worth carrying into the memo.
- **Windows operating system licensing** — substantial revenue from Windows licenses on PCs,
competing with smartphone/tablet platforms; users migrating functionality away from PCs;
competing operating systems licensed at **low or no cost** may compress PC OS margins.
Microsoft devices also compete with **its own OEM partners**, which may affect their
commitment to the platform.
- Disruption risk from changing user needs and frequent new product introductions.
## 2. Risks relating to the evolution of our business (line 677)

Covers the risk that the business model must keep evolving — cloud transition, AI adoption, and
related capital and execution commitments. **ASSUMPTION-flagged: I have not extracted the full

## 3. Cybersecurity, data privacy, and platform abuse risks (line 683)

**The single most concrete, dated, company-specific cyber disclosure in the filing — treat as
a standalone finding.**

**Disclosed incident (verbatim substance, line 690):** As previously **reported on Form 8-K
filed January 19, 2024 and amended on March 8, 2024**, beginning in **late November 2023** a
**nation-state associated threat actor used a password spray attack** to compromise a legacy
test account and, in turn, gain access to Microsoft email accounts. The actor used information
obtained to gain **unauthorized access to some of our source code repositories and internal
systems**, and **could continue to utilise this and other information** to attempt further
access or otherwise adversely affect the business. Microsoft states the incident **has and may
continue to result in harm to its reputation and customer relationships.**

**Diligence read:** this is a material prior intrusion reaching **source code repositories and
internal systems**, by a **nation-state** actor, with the Company stating the actor may *still*
have the ability to act on obtained information. For a target whose principal assets are source
code and AI models, that is a first-order technical risk. Note the reference is by **incorporation
by reference to the January 19, 2024 Form 8-K as amended March 8, 2024** — those filings are

**Further cyber risk content (line 690 onward):**
- **Nation-state and state-sponsored actors can sustain malicious activity for extended periods
and deploy significant resources.** Attacks may intensify due to Microsoft's **transparency**

- **Failure to update or apply security patches** to all hardware and devices connected to
Microsoft systems, **including end-of-life and end-of-support equipment**, may result in
unauthorised access. An enduring legacy-estate exposure.
- Threats are **constantly evolving and increasingly sophisticated**; actors use **AI and

machine learning** to increase speed and scale, generate malicious code, **automate
reconnaissance and targeting**, accelerate detection or exploitation of vulnerabilities and
rapidly iterate. This is material given Microsoft's own AI capability.

contain and remediate**; remediation efforts **may not be successful** and Microsoft **may

make errors or fail to take necessary actions**.
- It **may take considerable time to investigate and evaluate full impact**, meaning Microsoft
**may not be able to provide prompt, full and reliable information** about an incident to
customers, partners, suppliers, regulators and the public. A disclosure-timeliness risk.
- Threat actors **may gain undetected access to other networks and systems** after establishing

## 1. THE HEADLINE ITEM: $28.9 billion IRS transfer pricing assessment

This is, on the disclosed figures, **the single largest quantified contingent liability in
Microsoft's filings** — larger than the entire annual dividend, larger than two years of the
entire buyback programme, and roughly 21% of FY2026 net income before penalties and interest.
**Verbatim substance** (10-K, Note 14 — Contingencies, line 7589):

> "We remain under audit by the IRS for tax years 2014 to 2017. With respect to the audit for
> tax years 2004 to 2013, on September 26, 2023, we received Notices of Proposed Adjustment
> ('NOPAs') from the IRS. The primary issues in the NOPAs relate to intercompany
> transfer pricing. In the NOPAs, the IRS is seeking an additional tax payment of
> **$28.9 billion plus penalties and interest**. As of June 30, 2026, we believe our allowances
> for income tax contingencies are adequate. We disagree with the proposed adjustments and will
> vigorously contest the NOPAs through the IRS's administrative appeals office and, if
> necessary, judicial proceedings."

**Replicated in the 10-Q** at three separate places (lines 4753, 7452, 8126), confirming it
remains a live, current disclosure as of the quarter ended March 31, 2026 — not a stale

## 3. The substantive content: a change to two reportable segments

**Diligence read:** this materially reduces comparability of Microsoft's historical segment
disclosure. A buyer underwriting segment-level growth must rebuild the series on the new basis

The same caution applies to any forward-looking content in the investor materials: it is

Plan** (both are referenced in the share-limit provision).

- **Recycling mechanic:** Shares never again become available if they were (A) tendered or
withheld for taxes, (B) tendered or withheld to pay the Option exercise price, (C) repurchased

with Option exercise proceeds, or (D) underlying exercised SARs. Shares are authorized but

### Change of Control - this is the section the memo must cover in detail
"Change in Control" means any of:
- **(i) Board change:** Incumbent Directors (those constituting the Board at the start of a period
of not more than **36 months**) ceasing to constitute at least a **majority** of the Board. A
later-elected director counts as an Incumbent Director if elected/nominated by at least
**two-thirds** of the Incumbent Directors. Directors elected as a result of an actual or
publicly threatened election contest do not count.
- **(ii) 50% ownership:** any person becomes a beneficial owner of securities representing

**50% or more** of combined voting power. Carve-outs: the Company itself, employee benefit
plans, underwriters temporarily holding in an offering, and Non-Qualifying Transactions.
- **(iii) Business Combination:** consummation of a merger, consolidation, statutory share
exchange or similar transaction requiring **shareholder approval**, unless it is a
**Non-Qualifying Transaction** - i.e. the surviving entity (or ultimate parent holding at
least 95% of voting power) remains majority-owned by pre-transaction Company Voting
Securities **in substantially the same proportion**, no other person becomes a 50% beneficial
owner of the parent/Surviving Entity, and **at least a majority of the parent/Surviving Entity

board are Incumbent Directors** at the time the Board approved the initial agreement.
- **(iv) Asset sale:** consummation of a sale of **all or substantially all** of the Company's
assets (other than to an affiliate).

**Diligence read:** the acquirer-hostile protection is meaningful but not absolute. A topping-up
merger that satisfies the Non-Qualifying Transaction carve-out would **not** trigger the
acceleration/settlement machinery, and the asset-sale test excludes affiliate sales. This is a
standard-ish structure, not a deal stopper, but the 50% threshold and the board-departure test
mean a change of control is not automatic on a simple majority acquisition.

Cyberthreats are constantly evolving and becoming increasingly sophisticated and complex, increasing the difficulty of preventing, detecting and successfully defending against them. Our current capabilities may not detect certain vulnerabilities or new attack methods, which may allow them to persist in the environment over long periods of time. It may be difficult to determine the best way to investigate, mitigate, contain, and remediate the harm caused by a cyber incident. Cyber incidents and attacks can have cascading impacts that unfold with increasing speed across our internal networks and systems, as well as those of our partners and customers. In addition, it may take considerable time for us to investigate and evaluate the full impact of incidents, particularly for sophisticated attacks. As a result of these and other factors, we may not be able to provide prompt, full, and reliable information about the incident to our customers, partners, suppliers, regulators, and the public.
